discovery: Quantum simulation of many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Cirac and Zoller showed how precisely controlled atoms and photons can process quantum information. With Jaksch and colleagues (1998), they proposed that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model, which made atoms a programmable analog of strongly correlated electrons. Bloch's experiments realized this vision. In 2002 his group observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition, and his lab went on to pioneer controlled collisional entanglement, single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy, many-body localization and studies of out-of-equilibrium dynamics. Together, these works set up Feynman's quantum simulator as an experimental science. Many-body problems that cannot be solved classically can now be studied atom by atom. The field has grown into a worldwide effort that links condensed-matter physics, quantum information and metrology, and it underlies today's programmable neutral-atom quantum processors.
